full_judgment:
The facts leading to this writ petition are that the petitioner took loan amounting to Taka 3,37,343.06/= (Taka three lac thirty-seven thousand three hundred forty-three and Paisa six) only in the year of 1985-86 from Sonali Bank, Local Branch, Gaibandha for his business of raw jute processing. But at the very beginning of business he suffered huge amount of loss due to collapse of international jute market and thus became a defaulter. As a result the Sonali Bank, Gaibandha branch as plaintiff instituted Artha Rin Suit No. 87 of 1993 against him for recovery of the loan, which was decreed. Thereafter the decree-holder bank put the decree in execution by filing Money Execution Case No. 50 of 1994. There had been a ‘solenama’ in the said money execution case and the petitioner started paying off his loan in terms of the said ‘solenama’. But misfortune did not come alone, his wife passed away and he himself became paralyzed, for which he defaulted once again in payment of the outstanding dues according to the terms of ‘solenama’. After recovery from paralysis he had paid two more installments and started working hard by cultivating his land to arrange money to pay off his debt. Unfortunately a devastating Tornado swept away everything in his area on 19.3.2005 further disabling him in repayment of loan. Thereafter the petitioner requested the bank in 2006 to relinquish interest on the principal amount and to give him an opportunity to pay off the loan in the terms, what he agreed in the said execution case. On receipt of so many applications like the petitioner’s, the competent authority of Sonali Bank Ltd. took a policy decision to exempt the defaulting-borrowers of particular categories. In pursuance of the said decision, the vigilance and control division, Sonali bank head office issued circular No.1654 dated 1.3.2007 to its all branches directing for exemption of interest to the defaulting-borrowers, who borrowed less than five lac as principal amount of loan before 1995 and defaulted in repayment because of natural disaster, subject to filing of their respective applications within time agreeing for payment of principal amount plus 75% simple interest thereon and the cost of litigation. The Manager, Sonali bank, Gaibandha branch (respondent No.6) by a letter dated 13.3.2007 asked the petitioner to take the opportunity for exemption of interest within the scope of the said circular and accordingly he (petitioner) filed an application to that effect within time. The head office of Sonali bank referred the petitioner’s application to the General Manager with positive remarks. When the application was so pending before the General Manager, Sonali bank, Rajshahi office (respondent No.4), the Manager of its Gaibandha branch (respondent No.6) revived the aforesaid money execution case and attempted to take possession over his mortgaged property. In that event the petitioner served a notice demanding justice dated 19.8.2009 upon the respondents and getting no response, moved the High Court Division and obtained the instant Rule, and an order staying further proceedings in the execution case. 

 The Manager, Sonali bank, Gaibandha branch (respondent No.6) appears and contests the Rule by filling an affidavit-in-opposition contending inter alia, that the petitioner did not pay 75% of the outstanding dues in terms of the ‘solenama’ and therefore, he can not be exempted from his liabilities and get benefit under circular dated 1.3.2007.
